title: The Khalsa weighs mercy, honor, and saintly power

blocks.text: Once the first wave of anger settles, the assembly reflects on Bhai Taru Singh's spiritual authority and on the renown of the Panth. His words are treated as sharper than weapons, so any response must honor both justice and the Khalsa's public character.

Subeg Singh argues that a generous answer would magnify Sikh glory, because Divine Guru and Khalsa were synonymous with each other in the life of the devout community. The saints' power present in the Khalsa makes mercy meaningful precisely because it is not weakness.
The page thus turns from battle-talk to theological self-understanding. The Panth considers how to preserve both the authority of Taru Singh's curse and the higher reputation of Sikh compassion.
